q: About how many guided learning hours is the 0510 syllabus planned for?
why: The syllabus is designed around about 130 guided learning hours, but this is only guidance.

q: What does 'guided learning hours' mean?
o: Time a teacher spends teaching or guiding the student
Time a student spends on holiday
Time spent in the exam hall only
why: It is the time a teacher spends teaching or guiding students.

q: In which exam series can students normally be entered?
why: Students can be entered in June and November. Schools in India can also use March.

q: Which extra series is open to schools in India?
why: Schools in India can also enter candidates in the March series.

q: Who sends the entries to Cambridge International?
why: Exams officers are responsible for submitting entries.

q: Why do Cambridge schools have an administrative zone?
o: Each zone has its own exam timetable and papers
why: Papers and timetables are produced for different zones to keep exams secure.

q: Which of these can a student take together with 0510 in the same series?
why: Different subjects can be combined. The English-language syllabuses listed as exceptions cannot.

q: Can students retake the qualification?
o: Yes, as many times as they want
Only if they got grade G
why: Candidates can retake the whole qualification as many times as they want.

q: What is true about Speaking tests from an earlier series?
o: They cannot be sent in again, in whole or in part
They can always be sent in again
Only the interview can be reused
They are deleted by Cambridge after one day
why: Candidates cannot resubmit Speaking tests from a previous series.

q: In which language are the syllabus and assessment materials available?
why: This syllabus and its assessment materials are available in English only.

q: What is an access arrangement?
o: A change that removes a barrier for a student with SEN, disability, illness or injury
A way to make the exam easier for everyone
why: Access arrangements are reasonable adjustments that remove barriers without lowering the standard.

q: When should a centre check which access arrangements are available?
o: At the start of the course
why: Availability should be checked at the start of the course.

q: Which of these is NOT a condition for approving an access arrangement?
o: It makes the exam easier for the student
It has a reasonable cost and timeframe
It does not harm the security of the assessment
why: Arrangements must be reasonable and must not weaken the exam. They are not meant to make it easier.

q: What does the grade 'Ungraded' mean?
o: The work did not reach the standard for grade G
why: Ungraded means the standard for grade G was not reached.

q: Which letter on a statement of results means 'pending'?
why: Q means pending. X means no result.

q: How is Speaking reported where students reach the right standard?
o: Inside the A* to G grade
With the letters Q or X
why: Speaking is separately endorsed with grades 1 to 5.

q: Cambridge says grade C overall with Speaking grade 2 can be seen as roughly which CEFR level?
why: The syllabus states this combination can be considered equivalent to B2.

q: How long is Paper 1 Reading and Writing and how many marks does it have?
why: Paper 1 is 2 hours and 60 marks.

q: What share of the written grade is Paper 2 Listening?
why: Listening is 30 per cent. Paper 1 is 70 per cent.

q: Which statement about Paper 3 Speaking is correct?
o: It is internally assessed and externally moderated
It is marked only by Cambridge examiners
It is part of the written grade
why: The teacher marks Speaking and Cambridge moderates the marks.

q: Which assessment objective is about understanding implied meaning in reading?
why: R4 is understanding implied meaning.

q: Which writing objective is about the right register and style for the purpose and reader?
why: W4 covers register and style.

q: Reading quickly to get the general idea of a text is called:
why: Skim reading means reading fast for the general idea.

q: Which word shows contrast?
why: Although, however, whereas and in contrast show contrast.

q: Which text type is usually informal and published on a website?
why: A blog is usually informal and published online.

q: How many exercises are in Paper 1?
o: Six: four reading and two writing
Four: two reading and two writing
why: Paper 1 has four reading and two writing exercises.

q: How are the 15 marks for each writing exercise shared?
why: Up to 6 for Content and up to 9 for Language.

q: How many times do students hear each recording in Paper 2?
why: Candidates hear each recording twice.

q: In the Speaking test, which parts are assessed?
why: Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3 are assessed. The introduction and warm-up are not.

q: How is the Speaking test marked?
o: Four criteria (grammar, vocabulary, development, pronunciation) each out of 10
why: Each of the four criteria has a maximum of 10 marks, giving 40 in total.
